Sonet: ‘Fra bank to bank, fra wood to wood I rin’

Mark Alexander Boyd (1562–1601)

F
RA
 bank to bank, fra wood to wood I rin,
Ourhailit
 with my feeble fantasie;
Like til a leaf that fallis from a tree,
Or til a reed ourblawin with the win.
Twa gods guides me: the ane of tham is blin,
Yea and a bairn brocht up in vanitie;
The next a wife ingenrit
 of the sea,
And lichter nor a dauphin
 with her fin.
Unhappy is the man for evermair
That tills the sand and sawis in the air;
But twice unhappier is he, I lairn,
That feidis
 in his hairt a mad desire,
And follows on a woman throw
 the fire,
Led by a blind and teachit by a bairn.
